reddit.title: We rebuilt our EU DPP deadline page so every date comes from one file, not hardcoded copy
reddit.body:
Context: authichain.com/dpp tracks the EU Digital Product Passport (ESPR) rollout — the central registry, battery passports, textiles, and so on.

We rebuilt it so every date, status badge and meta description comes from one JSON timeline file instead of strings baked into the page at build time. A weekly automated regulatory-watch check updates that file, and the same file drives both the marketing page and the Cloudflare Worker that serves the production URL — one source of truth instead of two copies that can quietly drift apart.

Each milestone now re-labels itself (live / urgent / upcoming) against the current date, and the page shows a "Reviewed <date>" line so you can tell whether the data is current without taking our word for it.

It tracks published EU regulatory dates — it's not legal advice, and it deliberately won't guess a date the Commission hasn't set yet.

Curious whether others tracking ESPR/DPP deadlines for their own supply chain find a page like this useful, or would rather have the raw JSON/API directly.

Disclosure: I work on this project.
